claim: A zero-in-degree candidate not already retired is condemned by HEADing its blob, capturing its current token, and appending `(hash, token, K)` to the retired output; an absent blob is skipped.

`RunFileReader` has borrowed-memory and streaming modes; streaming mode retains only the footer index and one current block no larger than `kRunHardCapBlockSize` = 1 MiB, while `seek` uses a ranged GET for the target block.
When a GC-shard delta bucket is empty, the new `fold_seal` carries the parent generation's `RunRef` key and checksum verbatim and performs no run GET or PUT for that shard.
`RunRef` has an explicit additive `shard` field so consumers associate a run with a GC shard without parsing key paths; run consumers resolve through seal references rather than constructing keys.

Retention must preserve any run object referenced by the live adopted seal; when a later pass replaces a parent reference, it deletes the superseded old-generation prefix after the CAS, with a crash window that can strand at most one small object per shard in the original design.
A fold using an empty baseline must throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` when a discovered ref shard proves trimmed history: `journal.front().transition_version > 1`, or an empty journal with `shard_version > 0`.
The baseline guard gates GC only; it never blocks server startup or normal reads and writes, and a genuinely fresh pool whose journals start at version 1 passes.
`Gc::rebuildBaseline` writes only the GC plane—runs, seals, and `gc/state`—and never modifies ref shards, manifests, or blobs or deletes content.

Rebuild edge accumulation is bounded by a memory budget: per-GC-shard edges are sorted and spilled into temporary run segments, then merged into one run using the T2 streaming readers and `RunFileWriter`.

The rebuild mints `new_round = max(observed_gc_round over all mount bodies, fence_round over all shards, and surviving gc/gen prefix numbers) + 1` so stale acknowledgements cannot float fresh condemnations past the floor.

A successful rebuild publishes an empty `retired_refs` set, preserving the reconstructed snapshot and making all content pass through the normal condemn → acknowledgement floor → graduate → delete pipeline again.

The rebuild's per-shard guard is stricter than a global empty-baseline check: it fires for any shard with no sealed cursor whose journal proves trimmed history, while a shard born after the baseline passes because its journal starts at `transition_version` 1.

The snapshot-streaming implementation requires `RunFileReader` to have no whole-run member, keeps `cur_block.size() <= kRunHardCapBlockSize`, and bounds every ranged request by `kRunHardCapBlockSize + 64 * 1024` plus the footer allowance.
The intended streaming open profile is exactly one HEAD, one tail ranged GET, and one body `getStream`; `seek` adds one ranged GET per touched block.
A pure reference-carry path requires both an empty delta bucket and an empty retired-merge input; an empty delta with prior retired entries still runs the merge so retired entries settle every pass.

The raw rebuild API returns `RebuildReport` with `performed`, `refusal`, minted `round` and `generation`, counts for namespaces, shards, committed refs, live precommits, unowned-alive manifests, edges, and clamped shards.

DEFER leaves the sealed `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)` unchanged, so journals accumulate naturally from the old sealed cursor and a later FOLD processes the accumulated deltas without new persisted accumulator state.

The pre-fold DEFER decision uses only O(shards) `LIST(cas/refs/)` token-diff signals, O(retired-entries + servers) graduation-due signals, and an O(1) defer window; it does not read journals or inspect whether a changed shard contains `+1` or `−1` content.

A deferred owner removal is conservative because the stale in-degree is too high and can only delay reclaim, whereas a deferred owner addition is dangerous if a pending blob graduates from a stale zero in-degree snapshot.
A new zero-in-degree condemnation candidate discovered during DEFER is detected only at the next FOLD, delaying reclaim by at most the bounded defer window but never deleting an uncondemned blob.
`gc_fold_max_defer_rounds` bounds batching so every accumulated delta is folded within a bounded number of rounds; a due destructive decision also forces a FOLD.

The GC acceptance criteria require idle rounds to perform no generation-run reads or writes, small-delta rounds to amortize snapshot rebuilds, default behavior to remain unchanged except for idle skipping, and `dangling == 0` in unit and live validation.

`graduationDue` returns true for a retired entry with `delete_pending` or `condemn_round < min_ack`; a missing retired list also returns true to force the existing fail-closed fold path rather than silently deferring.
`changedShardCount` is the number of present shards whose token differs from the sealed generation, represented by the non-`DiscoverDecision::Skip` decisions from `computeDiscoverDecisions`.

A deferred GC round reports `RoundReport::deferred=true`, emits a round event with `outcome = "deferred"`, and leaves the sealed generation pinned without fold, delete, or round-commit CAS; a FOLD resets the leader-local defer counter.

A lower `observed_gc_round` caused by syncer lag is conservative because `computeHeartbeatFloor` takes the minimum acknowledgement across live heartbeats; lag can hold the floor back but cannot advance it beyond an installed round.
At steady state after driving GC to an idle deferred round, S34 measured zero discovery `CasRootGet` operations for iteration counts from 5 through 40 and flat `root_dirs = 2`.

Under S27 duplicate-key and dropped-continuation-token LIST anomalies, GC tolerated 40 perturbed LISTs with zero round errors, replica agreement, `dangling=0`, and dropped-content reclamation; unstable listings increased `CasRootGet` from 74 to 1373 as GC conservatively re-read.

`isPrecommitDead(uint64_t writer_epoch, uint64_t build_sequence, const MountLease & w)` must be shared by reclaim and discover paths; a future epoch is live, an older epoch is dead, and an equal epoch is dead only when the retired sentinel or `min_active > build_sequence` applies.
The force-Read fix must preserve `Skip` for a shard with no live precommit or a live-but-not-yet-dead precommit, and must be idempotent after the removal changes the shard token.

The force-Read guard is self-terminating: reclaim appends a removal, the shard token changes, the next round reads normally, and the shard becomes `Skip`-eligible after coverage no longer contains a live precommit.
Force-Read is strictly more reading than Skip and therefore cannot under-count in-degree; each abandoned precommit adds at most one forced revisit at the round its build sequence crosses the floor.
The resurrect supersede produces one retired entry per hash, drops the stale token entry, preserves hash order, and commits the replacement through the existing R5 round CAS.
A fresh upload is condemned only when the hash has been referenced, the current object exists, and its folded current in-degree is zero; never-referenced uploads are not condemned.
The CA cache disk shares the base disk's metadata-bound disk identity for GC scheduling and `system.content_addressed_log` attribution, so two disk names correspond to one GC identity.
`CachedPartFolderAccess::dropRefBestEffort` is `noexcept`, swallows cleanup failures, and relies on garbage collection to reclaim lingering debris.
Mutable files are not reachability state, and retained views hold no tokens with authority, do not affect GC in-degree, and do not protect objects from garbage collection.
GC journal-only mutations do not route through the facade and do not invalidate retained views because they do not change committed refs or committed `RootRef::mutable_files`.
After the precommit-removal mutation is durably committed, Build::abandon retires build_seq; the staged-manifest debris cleanup remains best-effort afterward.
Moving retireBuildSeq after precommit removal makes the precommit watermark-dead only after removal is durably committed, closing the double-removal window.
The dedup-adoption condemnation check remains safety-critical because adoption does not mutate the existing incarnation and a graduated delete can race an adoption that was not checked.
A durable precommit closure cannot be deleted by GC once a per-shard seal after precommitAdd folds the closure edge, because d becomes at least one and the entry is spared.
The per-shard seal is taken when the target shard is read, not once globally for the whole GC pass; the edge theorem still holds because the closure is stored in that target shard's journal.
A blob condemned after precommitAdd is doomed to be spared at the next fold, while a blob already graduated before precommitAdd must be detected by the writer and displaced with a fresh incarnation.
The K1 dedup-adoption gate is safety-critical: adopting an existing incarnation is invisible to GC's in-flight delete decision, so a condemned adopted blob must be displaced with a fresh incarnation.

GC condemn captures the body token and writes condemned meta, spare CASes condemned to clean, and delete removes the body by exact token before deleting the meta; there is no tombstone handshake in v3.
Mass-DROP metadata operations must use a bounded parallel pool because one million sequential metadata CASes at about 20 ms each would take roughly 5.5 hours.
GC writes condemned metadata at condemn, clears it at spare, deletes it after exact-token body deletion, and performs per-hash metadata operations on a bounded parallel pool.
GC deletion in the raw-body design is a tombstone handshake: transition meta from `condemned` to `tombstone`, delete the body, then delete the tombstone meta, using a bounded parallel pool.
A GC delete may delete a body only after winning the `condemned` to `tombstone` CAS; the terminal tombstone prevents a writer from re-establishing the body after that claim.
The destructive path fails closed: GC never deletes a body without a won tombstone claim, while a 404 during fold is recorded and continued rather than throwing or fail-closing the fold.

The committed-removal sweep must preserve a body after a `-1` removal is appended but before that removal is sealed by the GC fold, because the fold still needs the body to emit the decrement; the body becomes sweepable only after the removal is sealed.

GC condemns a clean meta by CASing it to condemned and stores the resulting condemned-meta etag in `RetiredEntry.token`; it spares by CASing condemned to clean and ignores absent or tombstone metas during the condemn pass.
Graduation is determined by `condemn_round < current_round`, where `current_round` is `new_round = state.round + 1`; using `state.round` would prevent entries from graduating.

GC supersede detection re-reads meta for net-zero-touched entries and compares the current meta etag with the stored condemned-meta etag; a mismatch means the retired entry refers to a newer incarnation.

The GC rebuild skips `.meta` keys in the `blobs/` listing, captures or repairs the corresponding meta for each body, and stores the condemned-meta etag rather than the body token in rebuilt retired state.
After a successful ref-fold adoption, consumed `_log` objects may be deleted in bounded batches; an interrupted post-CAS deletion leaves only physical debris and is not a second protocol phase.
Orphan cleanup protects current owners and every manifest removed in the unadopted tail using the exact adopted `RefBaseSet` plus the complete validated writer tail.

A live owner newly entering the fold requires a valid manifest body, an inherited-owner removal requires that body to emit `-1`, a move preserving the same `ManifestRef` emits no delta, and a missing required manifest aborts the entire GC attempt.

A productive ref handoff is forced by fold-delta threshold, ref-tail pressure, maximum defer age, destructive demand, or `remove_namespace`; a deferred round still replays the complete tail for destructive protection.
After a successful `gc/state` CAS, GC deletes covered ref-log objects with exact-key batch deletes of at most 1000 keys per request; if the CAS loses, it deletes no ref-log object.

The orphan-manifest sweep proves build retirement, reads the exact adopted `RefBaseSet`, replays the complete contiguous tail, rechecks `gc/state`, and deletes only candidates absent from the complete protection set.

Settlement semantics remain byte-for-byte unchanged in the retired-in-snapshot plan: condemn, carry, graduate with `delete_pending`, redelete, clamp suppression, pre-CAS single delete site, resurrect-supersede, `.meta` writes, B170 events, and GC-log counters are preserved.
A carried condemned sentinel is settlement-only: it never sets the merge touch bit, emits no zero marker, and does not trigger `peek_head` when carry is the only activity.

The 2-cursor settlement merge removes the separate `prior_retired` input: condemned rows are decoded from the prior source-edge run, settled at blob close-out, and emitted back at the blob's zero-sentinel key.
Fresh condemns emit `kCondemned` rows, absent-at-condemn cases emit `kZeroMarker` as before, prior zero markers are dropped on carry, and carried condemned rows do not set `cur_touched`.
With `suppress_destructive`, pending rows carry unchanged and floor-passed rows remain condemned-only, preserving the row bytes.
Every new fold seal contains a `condemned_summary` total over shards `0..gc_shards-1`; folding computes it from written condemned rows, while pure-carry shards copy the parent's entry verbatim.

For `snap_generation == 0`, `graduationDue` returns false; otherwise it reads the adopted seal and fails closed by returning true when the seal is missing, undecodable, or its summary is not total over `gc_shards`.

When the adopted seal summary is valid, `graduationDue` is true exactly when some shard has `pending_total > 0` or `oldest_nonpending_condemn_round < current_round`; it requires no backend GET beyond the seal read.

GC rebuild must first traverse journals and accumulate per-shard deltas and `edge_bearing`, then list physical blobs and head zero-edge bodies, mint condemned rows, append them to shard runs, seal summaries, and only then CAS `gc/state`.
The rebuilt orphan rows use `CondemnedRow{token, size, condemn_round = minted_round}` and graduate when `condemn_round < current_round`, which is the next round after minting.
A carried `kCondemned` row is settlement-only and must not set the merge touch bit; only real edges or deltas touching a blob may trigger a zero marker or a resurrect-supersede `peek_head` probe.
`CasFoldSeal` contains a per-GC-shard `condemned_summary` with `condemned_total`, `pending_total`, and `oldest_nonpending_condemn_round`, where `UINT64_MAX` means no nonpending condemned row.
A shard may be pure-ref-carried only when it has no deltas and `condemned_total == 0`.

`RetiredMergeResult` remains the interface for `graduated`, `spared`, `redelete`, and `replaced` outcomes, which continue to drive outcome logs, `.meta` transitions, B170 events, and `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, and `entries_redeleted` counters.
A crash between run PUT and seal or state CAS leaves orphan attempt-scoped artifacts that retention prunes through `snap_pruned_through` under B174.
The retired-in-snapshot design keeps B170 events, GC-log counters, `.meta` writes, and the `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` schema unchanged.

Settlement has no algorithm loop: rows are self-describing, `blobShard` uses the first eight digest bytes in big-endian order modulo `gc_shards`, and the algorithm is ignored only inside the shard calculation.
The fold seal remains total over `gc_shards` and gains no algorithm dimension or algorithm-driven partition iteration.
Condemn-sweep and fsck derive algorithm and digest width from the `blobs/<algo>/...` path segment; a segment not in `algos_used` is skipped by sweep and reported as `unaccounted` by fsck.
`blobShard` for variable-length digests is the big-endian uint64 represented by the first eight digest bytes modulo `gc_shards`, preserving routing for existing 128-bit digests.
GC stores one `last_folded_ref_id` cursor per table and manifest-edge deltas, not complete table state or owners; the cursor map is O(number of tables), not O(number of refs).
The `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` object is a zero-byte completion marker published with `putIfAbsent` after the exact namespace cleanup reaches `Completed`; Phase 1 never deletes markers.

The namespace-removal transaction emits no additional manifest-edge delta because its preceding exact owner transitions already emit all edge removals; its final operation creates the GC namespace-cleanup request.
GC performs one paginated global `LIST cas/refs/` per round for ref intake, snapshot observation, and cleanup planning; it does not perform per-table LISTs or snapshot HEADs.
Ref intake never directly deletes blobs or manifests; it only feeds appeared and disappeared edges to the existing multi-round GC settlement and delayed-delete protocol.
A ref log is eligible for deletion only when the durable per-table fold cursor covers it, a snapshot observed by the same scan covers it, and any namespace-removal cleanup work is durable.
Namespace cleanup has durable `Pending` and terminal `Completed` states keyed by `{namespace, remove_txn_id}`; `Completed` is written only after a pass observes no remaining objects to delete.

An orphan-manifest sweep uses the newest snapshot plus every later log, including manifests removed in the tail, and additionally requires the durable `last_folded_ref_id` before deleting a retired manifest.
GC ref-intake memory is O(one LIST page plus a bounded decoded transaction batch, emitted edge buffer, and retained exact cleanup keys), independent of table size.
A crash between copy completion and staging deletion may leak a staging object, which is reclaimed by a lease-fenced sweeper scoped to the mount's `staging/<mount_id>/` prefix and by GC age sweeps.
GC discovers blobs by listing `blobs/`, so it excludes `staging/`; the staging sweeper is the only reclaimer of staging objects and GC must not exact-token-delete them as orphan blobs.
`GC` never reads or GETs a condemned object to revive it; revival requires a fresh re-upload.

A 404 during `GC` folding is recorded and processing continues where the specification permits; where the specification requires fail-closed behavior, only the current attempt is aborted rather than the process.

Ref-delta intake uses paginated enumeration resumed after the last returned key, atomically adopts per-table candidate cursors in one fold commit, and adopts every durable log delta exactly once using event-id idempotence.
A losing ref-fold commit adopts nothing, and cleanup requires both cursor coverage and observed snapshot coverage.

`GC` performs one global paginated `LIST cas/refs/` with explicit start-after resume and persists per-table `last_folded_ref_id` cursors in the existing fold artifacts through the existing single `gc/state` CAS.

GC edge events are deterministic `+1/-1` events with `event_id={ns, txn_id, op_ordinal, edge_ordinal}`; same-manifest promotion has no net change, and add-plus-remove within one unfolded batch cancels.

Ref-object cleanup requires observed-snapshot coverage, cursor coverage, and item durability for removal transactions; cleanup uses exact keys, batches no larger than 1000, and can delete snapshots older than the newest observed snapshot.
Namespace cleanup items transition from `Pending` to `Completed` in fold artifacts; after `Completed`, GC publishes the `_cleanup` marker and republishes the `Removed` snapshot idempotently.

The orphan-sweep protection view combines the newest snapshot with the complete tail, protects owners and manifests removed anywhere in the tail, retains the young-manifest window, and requires the `last_folded_ref_id` condition.

`CasGcScheduler` must share one persistent `Cas::Gc` between `loop` and `runOneRoundNow`, serialize rounds with a dedicated `gc_round_mutex`, and protect lazy `gc_scheduler` creation with `gc_scheduler_mutex`.
The `suppress_destructive` decision for a GC round must be computed once in `Gc::fold`, stored in `FoldResult::suppress_destructive`, and reused by all destructive phases.

GC fence-out uses token-stability observation on the leader's monotonic clock: a non-terminated, non-fenced mount is fenced only after its token remains unchanged for `ttl + ttl / 20 + round_period_hint`, with a new leader starting with an empty observation map and therefore delaying fencing safely by one round.
GC fence-out uses token stability on the GC leader's own monotonic clock instead of comparing `MountLease.expires_at_ms` with the leader's wall clock.
The orphan sweep can report a `materialization_grace_ms` violation from a log below the seal without reading it to revive the object.

The §4 promote gate proves a future GC fold will spare an adopted blob after the destination precommit edge is visible, but it does not prevent a previously captured pre-CAS `deleteExact` from firing.
A resurrect displaces a condemned blob from token `t1` to fresh token `t2`, whereas `adoptEvidence` keeps the original token `t1` and therefore does not make a stale `deleteExact(h,t1)` harmless.
GC redelete runs before the round's `gc/state` CAS and does not re-check recovered in-degree before issuing `deleteExact` for a previously captured `delete_pending` row.
A fresh GC leader's spare is add-only and cannot cancel a stale leader's already-captured pre-CAS delete.
The GC defense audit found all six named GC-side sites compliant with the rule that foreign-writer defense spends no speculative S3 requests on hot paths.
The `gc/state` round-ownership re-read is used only for destructive namespace cleanup and checks both per page and per key to prevent mid-page namespace recreation.
Threading the already-held `(state, state_token)` pair to the terminal GC CAS avoids a zombie-steal re-read and costs zero requests.
The orphan-sweep eligibility gate uses the durable mount watermark to identify dead epochs and treats a missing watermark as not eligible, so it deletes nothing on that fallback.
Orphan-sweep `NotFound` and `TokenMismatch` outcomes are tolerated and logged without retries or re-verification GETs.
Fold-lag clamp barriers do not add request work: they defer cursor advancement and suppress graduation when manifest bodies are not yet visible.
When a listed ref-log body vanishes or fails to decode, GC aborts ref folding for the round and resets cursor advances to already durable parents without issuing diagnostic requests.

The Round-B plan defines `casSizedReadSettings` to shrink known-size fold read buffers to body size plus 4096 bytes, capped at the caller's base buffer size, while leaving unknown size zero unchanged.
The writer's GC retention floor is the minimum `S_min` over every non-expired reader pin and gates blob reclaim, ref-object cleanup, and namespace cleanup.
A dropped table or dead pool-member decommission does not reclaim a reader-pinned historical closure until the reader pin releases or expires.
Exact-token deletion protects against different-token resurrection but does not protect against same-token reuse.

`cas_gc_hb` is a full header'd text object with a header line and one JSON body line; its advisory owner and monotone `hb_seq` semantics remain unchanged, and the former 24-byte unversioned representation is removed.
`GcState.gc_shards` is immutable and must be at least 1; decoding a zero value raises `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

`cas_gc_outcomes` is line-structured as a header, one flat JSON record per `OutcomeEntry` in insertion order, and a `{"n":<count>}` trailer; it is always zstd-compressed and stored under a `.zst` key suffix.

`cas_fold_seal` is `PinnedRaw` and `Strict`; its encoder emits fixed field and section order, sorts vector collections by run key inside the encoder, and must be byte-reproducible for `putDeterministicArtifact` adoption.

The `cas_fold_seal` body consists of a header, a metadata line, record sections in coverage, blob-target-runs, part-manifest-cleanup, condemned-summary, and namespace-cleanup order, followed by a `{"n":<total record count>}` trailer; record kinds are `cov`, `btr`, `pmc`, `cnd`, and `nsc`.

A fold-seal `nsc` record reconstructs its map key as `ns + newline + renderRefTxnId(remove_txn_id)`; a zero `{0,0}` transaction id is invalid for `nsc`, while a zero `last_folded_ref_id` is allowed for coverage records.
`MetaState::Clean` means the blob is referenceable and present, while `MetaState::Condemned` means GC found zero in-degree but the body remains present and may be resurrected by a writer CAS.
The condemned-state gate remains correct when the text codec round-trips `state`, `condemn_round`, and `size`, because dedup and GC branch on decoded fields and CAS-swap by etag.
The `cas_run` object is the GC source-edge in-degree data plane and is converted from `CARN` block-framed binary to sorted NDJSON with a typed header, one record per line, and a {"n":count} trailer.

The part-manifest-cleanup run has no reader: actual cleanup executes inline from the in-memory `folded.mf_cleanup` map, so the durable cleanup run and fold-seal `part_manifest_cleanup` field can be removed without changing the delete driver.
The shared retention-overlay primitive folds current refs together with the edge sets of live-owner pins, and a blob is condemnable only when its source-edge set is empty across that union.

Retention pins may encode their protected edges as either an explicit manifest closure or a snapshot window; the primitive is agnostic to payload shape and distinguishes consumers by ownership and liveness.
The proposed reaper deleted `gc/fetch-pins/<srid>/<build_id>` when `build_id < srid.min_active` or when the owning `srid` was terminated, fenced, or lease-expired.

The CAS GC graduation rule must require confirmed durable `Condemned` metadata for the exact `(hash, token)`; absent confirmation carries the entry to the next round instead of deleting, without changing the rule that a 404 during fold must not throw.
Pre-CAS generation pruning must protect the union of generations referenced by both the proposed seal and the parent seal; only generations referenced by neither may be deleted before the CAS.

The emulated backend should derive `TokenType::Emulated` token values from the underlying local-object etag so list and head agree and a post-restart fresh incarnation cannot match a persisted exact-token delete.

GC keeps its asynchronous advisory metadata model, but graduation to `delete_pending` or redelete requires confirmed durable `Condemned` metadata for the exact `(hash, token)`; missing evidence causes a fail-safe carry.
The planned GC marker confirmation can come from a successful marker write in the current or earlier round or from a fresh `loadMeta(hash)` observing `state == Condemned && token == entry.token`.
Pre-CAS generation pruning must include every generation referenced by the parent seal as well as the proposed seal, because a losing leader must not delete a run referenced by the winning leader.
The CAS scheduler lifecycle fix must hold `gc_scheduler_mutex` across `runOneRoundNow`, reject lazy creation after shutdown, and synchronize `cas_store` and `part_access` reads with shutdown resets.
The access type for the renamed command is `SYSTEM_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GC_RUN` with grant string `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC RUN`, and the interpreter method is `runContentAddressedGcRun`.
`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC STOP` must stop future rounds and clear `i_am_leader`; `GC START` must resume rounds on the same scheduler while preserving `gc_id`.

After a successful confirm, GC cannot delete the referenced blobs before a later removal event because every fold that sees a post-confirm `-1` also sees the durable receiver `+1`, and a straddling fold spares positive in-degree rows.
CAS blob in-degree is a SET of source edges with last-wins semantics per key, not a counter; an unmatched removal is a per-key no-op and cannot remove a sibling manifest edge for the same blob.

The fsck `stale_edge` class is detail-mode only and should be emitted when every in-degree edge for a blob names an absent manifest; a blob remains ordinary `AwaitingGc` when any edge still names a present manifest.

A GC round enumerates the `cas/refs/` prefix twice: `Gc::preFoldRefScan` supplies the defer signal and `Gc::fold` performs the folding walk; only a hole in the fold walk reproduces the skipped-transaction defect.
The `BlobDelta` row remains 64 bytes when `txn_ordinal` is placed after `remove`, because the ordinal occupies existing tail padding; `kBlobDeltaSize` and a `static_assert` pin this hot-path size.

Probe A reports a disagreement only when a ref-log id is present in one enumeration, absent from the other, and strictly below the other enumeration's maximum id for the same namespace; this witness condition excludes normal concurrent appends.

Probe A cannot detect a hole reproduced identically in both enumerations or a namespace omitted wholesale from one enumeration, and widening the rule to use the pre-scan maximum as a witness was rejected because it can permanently block legitimate cleanup.

When Probe A detects a disagreement, ref folding is aborted for the round: cursors do not advance, accumulated deltas are discarded, parent cursors are carried into the seal, and destructive actions are suppressed.

Probe B1 compares a running count of logs applied at the single `resolved_through = log_id` cursor-advance site with a seal-time recomputation from sealed coverage and the ref listing; it is a control-flow assertion and is blind to a record missing from that same listing.
`TxnApplyLedger` is round-local and never persisted; it tracks each opened ref transaction, whether it produced deltas, whether intake committed it, and whether a reducer consumed at least one delta.

Probe B2 marks a transaction applied at reducer consumption rather than run flush, because the in-degree model is a set and legitimate unmatched removals or duplicate activations may disappear during set merging.
The garbage-collection log phase schema adds `EventType::Phase`, `round_id`, `phase`, `phase_duration_us`, and `phase_metrics` without removing or reordering existing fields.
The ref-log cursor is sealed above every record a GC round observed, not every record that exists; an omitted durable ref log can therefore never be folded by a later incremental round.
When Probe A fired, the round aborted folding, held the cursor, and a later complete enumeration folded the missing records; the three keys were deleted six minutes later and no leak resulted.

The in-degree reducer models source edges as a set: an unmatched `-1` is dropped as a no-op and a duplicate `+1` collapses, so the reducer must not materialize negative edges merely to repair the retention leak.

The durable fix requirement is that GC must not advance a cursor over records whose enumeration it cannot prove complete; the committed direction is an authoritative per-namespace chain plus a complete-cut gate.
Blob in-degree is pool-wide, so destructive GC rounds require a frontier proof for every catalog namespace rather than only namespaces returned by a listing.

The pre-fold drain takes a complete catalog snapshot, selects one eligible row, and restarts its complete scan after every CAS outcome; only a scan with no eligible row permits the invocation to continue.

The dead-life janitor enumerates `cas/ns/` separately from the fold's hot `cas/ns/stream/` LIST, takes one fresh catalog GET per page rather than per key, and deletes only after page-wide life revalidation and an exact fence/token check.

Janitor progress is stored in the leak-only `<prefix>/gc/maintenance_state` object registered as `FormatId::GcMaintenanceState = 25`; losing or repeating this cursor can repeat cleanup work or leak bytes, but cannot affect GC authority, frontier completeness, `DEFER`, catalog lifecycle, or successor publication.

A physical id returned by a completed LIST and absent from the corresponding later catalog cut is inert dead-life debris: the fold counts and drops it, while only the janitor may nominate its physical deletion.

Snapshots are deletable only strictly below `_ckpt.checkpoint`; a stale pointer can only under-clean, and a missing sampled base requires rereading `_ckpt` to distinguish a concurrent advancement from corruption.

After the mandatory pre-fold drain, the fold performs one strict `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, then one fresh full-catalog cut, and builds its sole ref plan from that cut plus the completed LIST observations.

Each catalog-admitted life is folded arithmetically from its adopted cursor through exact `_ckpt.committed_through`; an omitted life receives the same finite exact walk, while hint holes such as `0x1430c`/`0x1430d` are not correctness gaps.

A destructive round may perform condemnation, graduation, deletion, sweep deletes, or ref cleanup only after every `Live`/`Removing` catalog entry reaches its same-round `_ckpt.committed_through` frontier; missing checkpoints, incomplete walks, or budget exhaustion suppress all destruction.

A classification-4 `ShardCoverage` hold stores a bounded reason, offending position, and retry/backoff data per `(namespace, incarnation)`; `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete` is recomputed before every destructive site.

Every carried hold is pool-wide suppression because blob in-degree is pool-wide; a hold retries its exact offending position and clears only after that position is folded and the result is adopted in `gc/state`.

With healthy authoritative `gc/state`, REBUILD carries all holds verbatim; with missing or undecodable `gc/state`, REBUILD has authority to reconstruct only, performs zero catalog deletions, and returns.
A manifest from epoch E is deletable only after the cursor consumes epoch E's seal and no unconsumed tail record above the cursor names it as a removal target; any uncertainty retains it.

Orphan-manifest deletion accounts for the manifest's exact blob/source edges through a separate accounting-neutral retirement input, consumes no ref-transaction ordinal, and does not require every affected blob to have zero total in-degree.

Stage A hard-wires `frontier_incomplete = true` through `UniversePolicy::kDefault = StageA_Suppressed`, so `suppress_destructive` holds on every production round and all delete families remain inert until Stage B supplies the catalog universe.
Snapshots are deletable only strictly below `checkpoint_snapshot_id`; if a sampled checkpoint base is missing, a changed `_ckpt` token causes restart and an unchanged token causes `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

Fold arithmetic intake walks exact `expected = cursor + 1` keys rather than iterating `listing.logs`; a hint hole that GET finds is folded without anomaly, while a 404 with no higher witness marks the normal frontier.

Epochs are crossed only by consuming a seal at the expected id; an `EpochSeal` is counted as applied with `produced=false`, and a later-epoch record reachable before its seal is held rather than guessed across.
Per-namespace fold failures such as corrupt bodies clamp or hold that namespace, while the rest of the round continues; only a key unattributable to any namespace aborts the whole round.

`ShardCoverage` classification 4 requires `HoldReason`, `offending_position`, `retry_count`, and `next_retry_round`, and those fields are forbidden for other classifications; malformed hold grammar is `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A hold clears only after folding through its `offending_position` and adopting the result in `gc/state`; if an above-cursor witness disappears while the gap remains, the hold changes to `WitnessDisappeared` and remains held.

The fold's `DestructiveGate` requires a frontier proof for every known namespace; a quiet namespace is probed with one exact GET of `expected_next(cursor)`, and budget exhaustion suppresses all destruction even if safe cursor progress is published.

`suppress_destructive` is true when anomalies exist, a hold is carried, or the frontier is incomplete, and it must be consulted at every destructive site including manifest deletion, generation prune, orphan sweep, handoff reclaim, and ref cleanup.

The sweep's shared `manifestDeletionPremise` requires both consumption of the manifest's epoch seal and no unconsumed tail removal target; unreached frontier, budget exhaustion, or a hold retains the manifest.
REBUILD removes the old blobs-prefix condemnation path and condemns nothing; this deliberately leaves manifest-less orphan blobs unreclaimable until the separate build/upload registry work in R4.

Under the Stage A default, a namespace absent from both the hint and `gc/state` can hold an acknowledged shared-blob `+1` while another namespace exposes a `-1`, yet the required result is zero deletes because `StageA_Suppressed` prevents data loss.

The hot GC round completes one `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, then takes one authoritative full-catalog `{token, value}` cut; `Live` and `Removing` entries in that cut are admitted, while listed ids absent from the later cut are inert dead-life debris and are not admitted or a reason to defer.

Every GC invocation acquires and validates the lease and adopted seal, conclusively drains eligible `Removing` rows, completes `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, takes one fresh full-catalog cut, builds the ref walk plan, and only then decides `DEFER` or performs fold, seal, and adoption.

A complete `Removing` row may be exact-CAS-deleted only when the matching adopted parent life row contains cleanup evidence and no durable hold; ambiguous or conflicting catalog CAS outcomes are resolved conclusively before successor publication.

The perpetual janitor scans `LIST(cas/ns/)` in bounded pages, stores one cleanup-only opaque pagination token in `GcMaintenanceState`, and takes a fresh catalog read after each page before classifying and exact-token-deleting candidates.
A valid janitor page under destructive suppression does not advance its cursor, preventing alternating `DEFER` and fold rounds from permanently skipping a dead page.

Destructive cleanup of a current catalog life revalidates the life and fence immediately before every per-key `deleteExact`; the dead-life janitor may use a page-level catalog cut because catalog-before-object publication and non-reused `life_id` provide the stronger ordering proof.

The destructive gate remains `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete`; the Stage B change permits `frontier_complete` to become true from catalog proof but does not weaken any suppression term.

R3 orphan-manifest cleanup exact-GETs and decodes the manifest first, feeds its `BlobRef`s through a neutral nomination input, adopts nominations in the round's `gc/state` CAS, and only then performs exact-token deletion.
In the fold model, a page scan is only a hint that may omit keys; arithmetic `WalkStep` advances the cursor by expected transaction id and supplies the authoritative delta candidates.

The fold's blob in-degree is pool-wide and is computed from fixed `EdgeOf` roles over folded keys; condemnation requires every table frontier proof and no hold, while deletion also requires no hold and two-phase pacing.
The stale-leader cleanup model makes recreation safe structurally: stale deletes capture and target the old incarnation, while reuse of an incarnation is the sabotage that violates rebirth safety.

The orphan sweep's neutral nomination input is accounting-neutral: it does not consume ref-transaction ordinals or increment unmatched-remove accounting for an already-absent edge, while retaining exact source-edge identities.
Stage A sets `UniversePolicy::kDefault` to `StageA_Suppressed`, so every destructive GC site is suppressed by construction and no object is deleted during Stage A.

The destructive-gate suppression covers nine GC deletion sites: pre-CAS blob deletion, hand-off generation reclaim, owner-removed manifest bodies, generation pruning, orphan-manifest sweep invocation, covered-log and superseded-snapshot cleanup, namespace-cleanup pending work, `_ckpt` known-key deletion, and merge-side pending deletes.
The orphan-manifest sweep deletes only with seal-consumed and no-tail-removal evidence; when the evidence is uncertain, it retains the object.

REBUILD does not condemn objects that its traversal did not reach; a manifest-less orphan blob remains unreclaimable until register R4 can enumerate in-flight build/upload operations, and is reported by fsck as `unaccounted`.

The GC fold reads `expected = cursor + 1` by exact key, proves epoch crossings via `crossFromSeal`, treats a hint hole as a non-event, and turns an absent expected-next with a witness above it into a per-namespace HOLD with `ShardCoverage::classification == 4`.

A 404 while folding a body the round already decided to read is treated as a concurrent delete and recorded while the round continues; this behavior remains required because throwing would wedge GC for the pool.

`CaGcAckFloorCore`, `CaGcAckFloorZombie`, and `CaGcCondemnMarkerGate` assume a complete fold cut; v9 turns that assumption into arithmetic discovery plus a durable classification-4 hold, so an undeclared skipped suffix becomes structurally unrepresentable without rewriting those orthogonal models.

An unreleased binding becomes eligible when a successor epoch exists and is reclaimed by `sweepStalePrecommitsNow`; it is unbounded only while no successor mounts the namespace or every successor sweep fails, so a dedicated fsck class is unnecessary.

The relink TLA model must name `CommittedEdgesAreGcVisible`: a committed ref edge durable before a removal is appended must be observed by every GC fold that observes the removal; the v9 chain models are responsible for discharging it.
LIST may discover old namespace-file debris only for lazy cleanup; LIST omission may leak storage but must never affect file visibility, namespace rebirth, or deletion safety.
Cleanup retains the checkpoint base's matching non-seal `_log` while `_ckpt` names that base; older covered logs remain deletable.

Namespace-file cleanup removes `_files` from mandatory namespace-removal LIST deletion, uses exact-token deletion with the deposited incarnation, and never re-derives incarnation from the current catalog entry during resumed cleanup.
`Gc::foldManifestEdges` at `Gc/CasGc.cpp:1007-1018` performs one `backend.head(key)` followed by one `backend.get(key)` per manifest edge, and `CasRefManifestBodyFoldGets` counts the GET half.
Destructive GC is permitted only when `frontier_complete = true` and `suppress_destructive = false`; the suppression gate remains `anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete`.
The `Removing` to `RemovalReady` transition must refuse while a hold with `ShardCoverage::classification == 4` exists for the namespace.

A GC round whose catalog cut predates the `Removing` to `RemovalReady` CAS may write the cursor once more; the next round must prune it, and final deletion must revalidate the adopted seal and tolerate this one stale-cut round.
Cleanup must capture `NamespaceLifeId` at deposition and never re-derive it from the catalog during a resumed or stale pass.
A deposited cleanup item stores `NamespaceLifeId` and `remove_txn_id`, and every resumed or stale cleanup pass uses those captured values directly.

A pending cleanup item performs one bounded, suppression-aware, best-effort pass with exact-token deletion; `NotFound`, token mismatch, or LIST omission retains or defers work and never becomes a safety conclusion.

Terminal-owned manifests are cleaned from exact `ManifestId` values in the terminal record after decrements are durable; the removal pass does not LIST and delete the shared manifest namespace prefix.
GC may CAS `Removing` to `RemovalReady` only when the matching cleanup item is durably `Completed`; it must not infer completion merely from item absence.
A `RemovalReady` round does not probe, fold, carry, or recreate the namespace cursor, and removes the matching completed cleanup item and shard-0 cursor together in the adopted seal.

The `_cleanup` marker can be removed because stale cleanup targets only the deposited life-qualified ref and `_files` prefixes or exact old terminal-owned manifests, never a namespace-wide prefix that a new life can create.
The catalog admission reservation must cover non-per-namespace seal data such as `blob_target_runs` and `condemned_summary`; entry ordering does not remove those capacity terms.
An absent canonical life is inert debris and must never become a pool-suppressing damage anomaly.
After probe A removal, each folding round must perform exactly one full `cas/ns/stream/` enumeration; the bounded `cas/ns/` janitor page is counted separately.

The destructive gate formula is `frontier_complete = universe_authoritative && frontier_namespaces > 0 && frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces` and `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete`.

The destructive gate has five independent suppressors: non-empty anomalies, non-empty carried holds, `!universe_authoritative`, `frontier_namespaces == 0`, and `frontier_proven != frontier_namespaces`.

Per-round GC work caps must leave excess work in the durable pipeline for later rounds, never drop or re-derive it, and the per-key row/life/lease validation before each exact delete must not be amortized or weakened.

Orphan-planner budget exhaustion must fail closed by retaining candidates, recording a counted retained cause, and leaving the cursor before the first undecided key; every round must either decide at least one candidate or advance the cursor.
`deletePrefixWholesale` and cleanup families must consume the round budget, and `snap_pruned_through` may advance only after a prefix is fully drained.
Injected holds or anomalies must leave every irreversible delete family inert for their rounds while the round still completes.
A missing attribution in orphan nomination must suppress destructive work rather than select a fallback owner.
The perpetual dead-life janitor owns namespace-life debris, while the orphan-manifest sweep owns orphan manifest bytes; both are cleanup mechanisms rather than identity or rebirth gates.

`INV_NO_RETIRE_UNCERTAIN_GRANT` prevents a writer cleanup duty from disappearing while the grant outcome is unknown; successor cleanup remains the seal-derived path for durable precommits left by a dead predecessor.
Exact GET and decode nominate an orphan manifest as a neutral candidate without consuming a B2 ordinal or entering unmatched-remove accounting.
`CommitRound` adopts an orphan nomination in the round's `gc/state` CAS, and only an adopted nomination may reach exact-token manifest deletion.

If a process dies after orphan-nomination adoption and before manifest deletion, the manifest remains leak-safe and rediscoverable; the protocol does not promise that the dead process retries deletion.
The perpetual `NamespaceJanitor::runOnePage` is invoked every GC round, is bounded by `page_budget`, is fenced by `gc/state` lease owner and sequence, and is leak-only.

Ref cleanup reads the authority from `folded.catalog_cut` rather than re-resolving it, and the `CasRefGcCleanupAuthority` tests cover catalog-token and GC-fence moves before the first delete and between two deletes.
CAS decommissioning rejects a `Removing` row without its `_ckpt` object with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, resumes a `Removing` row through `admin->dropNamespace(life)`, and leaves catalog deletion to GC.
CAS decommissioning requests a GC round after partial progress via a `request_gc_round` callback guarded by `SCOPE_EXIT`, including fail-closed exits.
`UniversePolicy::kDefault` remains `StageA_Suppressed`; `AuthoritativeForTest` is the test-only policy value read by `Gc::fold` to set `universe_authoritative`.

The destructive frontier gate is complete only when `universe_authoritative` is true, `result.frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `result.frontier_proven == result.frontier_namespaces`; anomalies, carried holds, or any incomplete frontier suppress destructive work.

Orphan-manifest nomination exact-GETs and decodes the captured body, validates `refMatchesBody` and `manifestNamespaceMatches`, derives `BlobSourceRetirement` entries, and performs no deletion during planning.

Orphan source retirements are passed to `foldDeltasIntoGeneration` as a vector distinct from the `BlobDelta` stream, preserving accounting neutrality; exact deletion occurs only after the round's `gc/state` CAS and only when destructive work is not suppressed.
GC driving uses one leader via `gc.gc_round` or `gc.gc_drive_round`; callers must not drive both leaders concurrently because that can cause a concurrent-leader reclaim leak.
In `ca-fsck` vocabulary, `dangling` means referenced but missing and is the INV-NO-LOSS data-loss class, whereas `unreachable`/`awaiting-gc` means present, unreferenced, and awaiting reclamation.

The middle of a ref-log enumeration remains arithmetic on every backend because predecessor omission below a correct paginated LIST tail is legal under concurrent writes; held namespaces and namespaces with no listed logs must still use the probe.

The unmatched removal-fold `-1` is harmless under the current edge-set model because source edges are set membership keyed by `(ref, ManifestId, path)`, not a counter; erasing an already-absent edge cannot affect another manifest's edges.

A regular GC round is all-or-nothing: `fold` produces one `gc/state` CAS followed by cleanup, and cleanup occurs only after the commit point because a durable `Removed` snapshot must precede deletion of covered logs.
`foldManifestEdges` returns false without deltas when a manifest body is absent, and the caller is intended to clamp the table rather than abort the round or advance its cursor.

The manifest-cleanup GC phase is a one-shot pipeline: its `-1` edge is consumed in the same CAS that produces `mf_cleanup`, so a per-round cap can permanently skip entries rather than defer them to the next intake.

Unadopted GC attempts are invisible to readers, resume, prune, and `RetireView`, so a deposed leader cannot collide on a final-key seal; unadopted attempt debris is reclaimed by wholesale `gc/gen/<g>/` retention pruning.
GC condemnation is fail-closed: a candidate absent at condemn time, including a HEAD 404, is skipped and no token is fabricated.

A missing or invalid committed/promoted new-binding manifest body clamps the affected GC shard with `classification = 4`; precommit bindings are non-activating, old-binding removals use fold-sealed edges, and GC never reads a deleted manifest body.

The GC publish-order invariant requires the retired-list runs for round K to be durable before the single `gc/state` CAS publishes `round := K` and `retired_refs`; refs and round are published together so round K always has a loadable retired list K.
A patch-part manifest is a first-class reachability root that keeps both its delta blobs and the referenced base blobs alive transitively.

The physical GC destructive gate is open only when the universe is authoritative, the frontier namespace count is nonzero, the proven frontier equals the namespace universe, and neither anomalies nor carried holds suppress destruction.
The ref-log intake walk still issues the exact-key `GET` at `cursor + 1` even when `cursor == tail`; an absent expected-next key with no higher witness is the proof that sets `frontier_proven`.
The delete guard in `GComplete` must force a fold for any pending delta touching the candidate blob, and `unfolded` carries both `add` and `del` signs.
A newborn shard is fenced to the current `gcRound` at birth, and GC discovers and fences every present shard by LIST each round.
When probe A detects a ref-scan disagreement, the fold must abort without advancing the cursor or deleting anything; the live detector stopped all seven observed folds this way.

Before any fold, `REBUILD`, or `DEFER` decision, the production GC actor must read the currently adopted parent seal, drain every eligible catalog row, conclusively resolve every exact CAS, and take a fresh catalog cut.
`CatalogTargets` must be derived only from the exact `Live`/`Removing` catalog plan key set, and `BeginRound` must freeze exact `_ckpt.committed_through` as `roundCte`.
`WalkStep` may exact-read only keys through the inclusive `roundCte` bound.
If a required key at or below `roundCte` is missing, the fold must reassert a hold without consulting `maxSeen` or any `LIST` observation.
`ScanComplete` may succeed only after every catalog target reaches CTE or resolves as held.
A target held at the start of a fold round must follow the same resolution path even when `LIST` returns no information.
`CteExact` requires `committedThrough[t] = MaxDurable(t)` for every table, and `RoundCteNoRegression` requires `roundCte[t] <= committedThrough[t]`.
`HoldReleaseRequiresFold` requires that no fold debt remains before a hold can be released.
The `cas/ns/` janitor must capture the exact physical life id encoded in a returned `LIST` key and continue targeting that id when a delayed delete resumes after same-name rebirth.
The janitor must not re-resolve a logical name at delete time; exact physical identity captured at nomination is the safety boundary.
Fresh life-id allocation and physical-id capture are independent requirements: reusing an id or re-deriving the target from the logical name can delete a live successor's data.
A janitor nomination is valid only when it came from an actual listed physical id; `NominationCapturedPhysicalId` checks this provenance.

Before `DEFER`, ordinary fold adoption, or `REBUILD` adoption, GC actor B must read the authoritative parent, resolve every eligible exact catalog CAS, complete the hot-stream `LIST`, take one fresh authoritative catalog cut, and build the ref-walk plan.
An old catalog request that returns after lease takeover is safe only if the successor actor consumed the token first or no successor invalidated the proof under which the old request lands.
A ready parent cannot proceed to normal fold, `REBUILD`, `DEFER`, or a fresh-cut continuation while an eligible catalog deletion remains unresolved.
If an exact catalog row is still `Removing` after an ambiguous or conflicting storage result, the actor must refresh the full-catalog token and retry; only an absent row is conclusive completion.

A missing or undecodable authority cannot be replaced by a seal discovered through enumeration for catalog deletion; honest `REBUILD` restores authority and returns, leaving the drain to a later invocation.
The authoritative catalog cut used for ref-plan intake must be taken after the completed hot `LIST`; a cut taken before `LIST` can omit a current successor and classify it as dead debris.
A predecessor listed later but absent from the authoritative cut is counted once, excluded from the life-id plan, and must never be used as a `DEFER` reason.

`IntakeConsumesFreshPostDrainCut` requires ref-plan intake to consume the exact token/value pair exported by `TakeFreshCut`, including life id and lifecycle state, and its plan projection must equal the walkable life-id set.
An exact delete or external catalog resolution that invalidates the full-catalog token requires a complete serial rescan before the next candidate or successor decision.
The all-row pre-fold drain may decide only when its remaining eligible-row set is empty; `CompletionDrained` defines `phase = "done" => remaining = {}`.

GC may delete a ref log only when `_ckpt` covers it; deleting a durable id below an unchanged checkpoint token makes a 404 indistinguishable from the frontier and can cause recovery to seal over adopted data.
Snapshot cleanup may delete only snapshots strictly below the current `_ckpt` base; deleting the snapshot still named by `ckpt.base` must fail closed as corruption after exact-key revalidation.
In-degree is a set-presence merge keyed by `(blob, source_id)` and applied in strict transaction-id order; a `del` whose key is absent is a silent no-op.
The in-degree reducer must not be changed to fix stale edges; the defect is upstream in the orphan-sweep premise.

The GC protocol includes leader election and lease, fold → retire → fence → recheck → trim/reclaim rounds, orphan removal through source-edge in-degree, exact-token deletes, shard incarnation, attempt-scoped generations, and snap pruning.

The canonical GC core requires exact-token deletion, atomic cascade with deletion, registry fencing from the committed namespace universe, and fresh observation of stale dependency evidence before publication.
A GC round that held back an unreadable shard must make no destructive decision, and the clamp-suppression guard prevents physical deletion while an unfolded delta could still touch the blob.
Two-phase graduation publishes `delete_pending` with a round CAS before physical delete, preventing a deposed leader's stale pass from deleting a live blob.

A durable never-reused per-shard incarnation plus a newborn shard fenced to the current GC round replaces the namespace registry's safety role, but reclaim still waits for the shard journal to be fully folded.
A due GC graduation must force a fold before physical deletion, while a non-destructive round may re-adopt the sealed in-degree snapshot; deferral is bounded.
Graduation to `delete_pending` requires confirmed durable `Condemned` evidence from a write-completion callback or synchronous meta re-read; otherwise the entry carries to the next round.

The pool-wide ref-delta fold makes every catalog `Live`/`Removing` life a mandatory target, snapshots exact `_ckpt.committed_through`, walks arithmetically to that bound, and treats every missing required key as a durable hold independent of `LIST`.

A pre-fold GC invocation must resolve all eligible exact catalog CAS operations, complete hot `LIST`, take one fresh cut, and build the sole ref plan before fold, `REBUILD`, or `DEFER`; ambiguous results cannot be treated as completion.
The perpetual namespace janitor captures a physical life id from a `LIST` page and delayed deletion never derives its target from a reborn logical name.
CAS GC computes blob in-degrees from manifest-to-blob source edges, condemns zero-in-degree blobs, and later deletes them with exact-token conditional deletes so a concurrent re-upload wins.

A GC round takes or renews the leader lease, collects source edges, folds per-shard in-degrees, condemns new zero-in-degree blobs, exact-token-deletes previously condemned blobs whose state is unchanged, and seals the round with one CAS on `gc/state`.
After forced GC, `unreachable` must be zero unless a scenario deliberately abandons writes; any residual must be classified by object class and proven bounded and expected.

S03 requires idle GC duration to scale with changed owner transitions rather than total live blobs, with `CASBlobList` equal to zero in regular journal-driven rounds unless an orphan sweep or `fsck` intentionally lists blobs.
S05 requires idle tables not to dominate GC CPU or S3 GET counts; ref body reads must be driven by new logs since per-table cursors rather than table count, and cursor regression must be reported.
S16 requires resurrection to use writer-owned source bytes rather than a condemned object, and requires `blob_reuse_resurrect` to fire at least once during the hot-content cycle.
Two-phase graduation uses `delete_pending`: pre-CAS deletes apply only to previously published pending entries, and deletion lags condemnation by one pass.
Every per-round GC artifact is keyed by `(gen, attempt = lease.seq)`, so artifacts from a deposed leader remain under an unadopted attempt.

The retired-in-snapshot design stores condemnation state as `kCondemned` sentinel rows in the source-edge run and stores per-shard `condemned_summary` in the fold seal; the merge therefore uses two cursors instead of three.
An empty-delta and empty-retired GC shard is pure ref-carry and performs zero run-object I/O; `RunRef` carries `shard` and `generation` and consumers resolve runs through seal refs.

Phase 4 Lever A lets a GC round re-adopt the sealed in-degree generation as DEFER when cheap pre-fold signals show no destructive decision; due graduation forces a fold, and the safety gate is `CaGcRoundDeferCore`.
When any shard is clamped, GC performs no graduation and no pending deletes; a clamp-free pass resumes deletes and emits a `gc_fold_clamp` event.

After removal of `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget`, the `manifest_deletes` phase drains all of `folded.mf_cleanup` unconditionally; the `skipped_budget` metric was dropped because it became structurally zero, while `attempted`, `deleted`, and `suppressed` remain.
GC journal trimming and abandoned-precommit reclaim do not change committed `root.refs`, so they do not invalidate part-folder views.
Cached views are not owner state, do not affect in-degree, and do not protect objects from GC.
CAS garbage collection is a background reachability process driven by an incarnation-token protocol using compare-and-swap on opaque storage tokens and failing closed.
`Cas::Gc` runs leader-paced reachability rounds with lease handling, crash resume, and precommit reclaim across fold, retire, fence, recheck, cascade, and trim phases.
`Cas::RetireView` is a thread-safe read-side mirror of condemned tokens consulted by the publish gate.
`Cas::RootsRegistry` is the authoritative namespace universe and GC `fence_round` record stored at the key `gc/registry`.
A GC round threads `(GcState state, Token state_token)` through its phases, re-CASes that state, and never re-reads it to preserve the anti-zombie invariant.
The GC round sequence is fold, retire, fence, recheck, cascade-and-persist, and journal trim; physical content deletion occurs at the recheck delete site.
The `lease` phase is the only phase emitted by a `NotALeader` round.
The `pending_deletes` phase is the single content-delete site for exact-token deletes of previously published `delete_pending` entries.
The `namespace_cleanup` phase performs bounded physical reclamation under `cas/ns/` and is not a lifecycle gate.
In `system.cas_log`, `round`, `generation`, and `at_version` are zero when not applicable, with `at_version` representing the driving manifest shard version.
The GC round asserts snapshot and journal coherence with the `B140-dangle` fail-closed guard before retiring candidates.

Stage A Task 9 must test same-round no-delete after a post-probe +1, SOURCE-BACKED/TOKENED rematerialization with stale-token delete refusal, and TOKENLESS receiver-plus-one-before-source-release ordering
The destructive-call inventory must include pre-gate handoff_reclaim, transport suppression before it, and add an individual zero-delete-under-hold test for every discovered delete family
Terminal fold cleanup must make one bounded suppression-aware best-effort attempt before exact _ckpt and catalog deletion, defer failure as leak-only janitor work, and assert backend-journal ordering
Current per-key deleteExact operations require catalog-token and fence revalidation before each key, with a credential-change race injected between two keys
The late-plus-one test needs an isolated seam that bypasses the final in-degree read, records RED, restores the guard, and records GREEN
GcStateProto.retired_refs is semantically load-bearing for the ack-floor writer gate; an old reader cannot safely ignore it without a compatibility gate or documented mixed-version rule
GcHeartbeat is exactly 24 bytes: a 16-byte big-endian GC owner id followed by an 8-byte big-endian heartbeat sequence, with no magic or version field
A cas_fold_seal contains rfl ref-life rows, sorted btr blob-target RunRef rows, and shard-sorted cnd condemned summaries, followed by a record-count trailer

Quarantine metadata must persist first-held round, retry generation, next probe, and offending anchor, and suppress_destructive must remain true for carried quarantine until successful revalidation
Every manifest named by an unconsumed removal record must be retained until the fold cursor passes that removal record, unless the blob-edge decrement is persisted independently of the manifest body.

Removal-tail protection scans must share the common round budget, cache decoded protection across candidates in a namespace, and retain every affected candidate when the authoritative frontier is not reached.
Every destructive round must exact-GET cursor+1 for every Live or Removing catalog entry and suppress all destructive work if the common budget expires before every namespace has a frontier proof.

A carried hold must persist {Held, reason-code, retry/backoff state} per (namespace, incarnation), force an exact retry without a hint, and suppress pool-wide destruction until a successful frontier walk or explicit operator repair clears it.

A forced REBUILD with a readable prior seal must carry every hold verbatim into the new baseline; a missing or undecodable prior hold authority must cause a pool-wide destructive hold or refusal, never an ordinary deletion-capable baseline.
A successful frontier walk clears a hold only when folding through the offending position and adopting that result in gc/state; reaching another absent expected-next does not clear it.

Classification 4 requires bounded hold fields and forbids those fields for other classifications; unknown, duplicate, or invalid field combinations must be rejected.
Every fold-seal PUT must verify encodeFoldSeal(...).size() <= fold_seal_cap, with the reservation estimator accounting for JSON escaping and framing.

An immutable node that landed but was never installed into _head is inert garbage with no owner semantics and is never folded.

GC exact-reads ref_catalog and every namespace _head, follows each sampled tip back to its exact cursor, and suppresses all destructive work when the cursor is not an ancestor or a node is missing, malformed, or over budget.
A safe GC cursor equals a sampled authoritative head, and every node on the unique path from the old cursor to that head has been exact-read and folded.

Snapshot cleanup may delete a listed node or snapshot only when point-readable facts prove the GC cursor covers it, the current head checkpoint covers it, and it is neither the current tip nor current checkpoint.

The orphan-manifest sweep protects every current committed or precommit manifest and every removed manifest named by exact chain nodes above the GC cursor, and deletes only a listed eligible manifest with its exact current token.

REBUILD exact-reads the catalog and every head at a sampled tip, emits baseline +1 edges for current owners, sets baseline cursors to sampled tips, refuses missing committed manifests or broken chains, and publishes with destructive work suppressed.
A physical blob LIST during REBUILD may nominate zero-edge blobs for condemnation, but omitted blobs remain leaked and are not treated as proof of absence.

`Cas::Gc`'s fold LISTs `casRefsPrefix()` and never `rootsPrefix()`, so `_files` keys do not reach a GC round even though `ContentAddressedTransaction::removeRecursive` handles both the ref-`_log` and `_files` key families.

`ns_cleanup_items` is keyed by `{ns, remove_txn_id}`, and a namespace can retain multiple `nsc` rows because rows retire only after a later round observes completion artifacts; a ref-folding abort skips retirement.
The `btr` per-run-segment rows and `cnd` per-gc-shard rows are charged neither in `worstCaseEntryFoldReservationBytes`'s fixed term nor in its per-entry term.
`Pool::listNamespaces` remains LIST-based and was not changed by the catalog-authoritative `Gc::discoverUniverse` switch.
In the T1/T6a frontier logic, the `checkpoint_unusable` anomaly bucket represents the no-cursor mechanism; an unreadable `_ckpt` when a cursor exists is reported as `held` instead.
`GcRoundWorkBudget::max_sweep_namespaces` counts cumulatively per round, not per PAGE; the two interpretations coincide only while a sweep takes one page per round.
The grounded `CasListLiarEndToEnd` fixture writes recoverable checkpoints for `hidden` with `committed_through = RefTxnId{1,1}` and `visible` with `committed_through = RefTxnId{1,2}`.
The list-liar test's load-bearing property is that `Gc::fold` reads each expected ref-log or checkpoint by exact key, so a LIST omission cannot make a durable edge appear absent.
The `CasGcFrontierGate` exact-key arm finds a hidden edge and saves its blob on a complete frontier; the round is not refused merely because the edge was hidden from LIST.

The GC log's `phase` column has these 18 execution-order values: `lease`, `pre_fold_ref_drain`, `heartbeat_floor`, `defer_decision`, `parent_seal_read`, `fold_ref_group`, `fold_seal_read`, `fold_ref_intake`, `fold_reduce`, `fold_seal_write`, `pending_deletes`, `meta_pool_wait`, `round_commit`, `handoff_reclaim`, `manifest_deletes`, `namespace_cleanup`, `ref_object_cleanup`, and `orphan_sweep`.
Logs for one table must be folded in strict ID order, and a clamp must stop that table at the correct log; prefetching may change only when data is available, never what is applied.
Each `deleteExact` carries its own token and must remove only the matching object incarnation, preserving GC safety against deletion of a replaced incarnation.
Observed LIST holes are short adjacent runs of 2–15 keys rather than approximately 1000-key pages, so completeness logic must not assume page-shaped holes.
The build watermark `build_seq` must be monotone; a non-monotone sequence can move `min_active` backward and re-protect a condemned blob, causing a leak.

Production destruction was suppressed in Stage A because pool-wide blob in-degree could contain an acknowledged `+1` from an invisible namespace while a visible `-1` was folded; suppression may be lifted only after the namespace universe is authoritative.
The source-edge reducer treats in-degree as a set: an unmatched `-1` must be dropped rather than materialized as a negative edge, because a negative edge could cause a false deletion.

A regular GC round acquires a lease, computes a heartbeat floor, folds shard journals into attempt artifacts, performs only previously published `delete_pending` deletes, publishes retired-list runs, and advances all state with one `gc/state` CAS.
`computeHeartbeatFloor` treats transient or unreadable mounts as live and holds `min_ack` down; only causally dead mounts are excluded, so injected S3 faults cannot raise the graduation floor.

`deleteExact` propagates transient, throttle, and authentication errors instead of forgetting the entry, while `TokenMismatch` and `NotFound` remain terminal outcomes for the exact-token deletion attempt.

If a lost acknowledgment follows a committed GC `gc/state` CAS, the retry reports `ABORTED`, while the next round reads the already advanced state and treats the earlier exact-token deletes as terminal and safe.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` reconstructs per-shard fold cursors and blob in-degree from owner shards and journals, and its baseline guard raises `CORRUPTED_DATA` when trimmed history cannot be accounted for.
The decommission sweep retains manifests when epoch 1's closing seal is not consumed, leaving them to normal GC; this can produce nonzero `unreachable` with `dangling=0` and no data loss.
`SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` writes only the GC plane, namely `gc/state` and `gc/gen/*` artifacts, and does not touch ref shards, manifests, or blobs or delete anything during the rebuild itself.

`SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` is a writer operation that emits ordinary ref-edge deltas and does not synchronously reclaim shared blob content; removing the edges makes those blobs eligible for a later ordinary GC round.

The GC implementation must use the same complete catalog cut for a decision and must not perform an independent catalog reread; the deleted `resolveLifeOrSentinel` helper was replaced in comments by this invariant.
The `CasRefGcCleanupAuthority` tests pin current-life destructive per-key `deleteExact` revalidation in the GC/cleanup layer; those class-3 catalog reads are not `CasRefLedger.cpp` sites.

When decommission reaches a Removing state before a later namespace fails closed, a SCOPE_EXIT callback preserves the GC liveness signal by invoking request_gc_round; the callback only wakes the serialized GC worker and does not perform catalog work.

Under the current Stage-A posture, Gc::runNamespaceJanitorPage passes the suppression flag to NamespaceJanitor::runOnePage, which visits unresolved physical life keys but skips every deleteExact when deletes are suppressed; canonical dead-life residue therefore remains pending until destructive rounds are enabled.

parseNamespaceFileKey now throws on dirty _files keys; NamespaceJanitor::runOnePage catches the exception, records an anomaly, and advances the cursor without clearing page_decided, so malformed keys do not wedge the janitor.

A rejected precommit body can be nominated and physically swept through real Gc::runRegularRoundReclaiming rounds after successor recovery closes the dead epoch with an arithmetic seal; genuine rejection means ChunkFaultBackend::Mode::Unresolved throws before CountingBackend::putIfAbsent.

The production default UniversePolicy::kDefault is StageA_Suppressed; a suppressed runRegularRound() does not call planManifestCursorPage, emits an orphan_sweep phase with listed == 0, deleted == 0, and suppressed == 1, and leaves the candidate manifest intact.

runFsckImpl classifies Creating, Live, and Removing catalog entries as protecting a physical candidate when CatalogLifeIndex::resolve returns a value, because the reverse index includes every catalog entry regardless of state.

The orphan-sweep watermark floor is derived from the namespace's own prefix segments and a live mount lease; a namespace rooted outside the pool's server_root_id is permanently ineligible for sweeping regardless of epoch or coverage.
After probe-A deletion, `Gc::RefScanSummary` retains `changed_shards`, `keys`, `listed_lives`, `logs_by_life`, and `max_log_by_life` because each field has consumers outside `sampleRefListQuality`.

The 18 GC phases execute in this order: `lease`, `pre_fold_ref_drain`, `heartbeat_floor`, `defer_decision`, `parent_seal_read`, `fold_ref_group`, `fold_seal_read`, `fold_ref_intake`, `fold_reduce`, `fold_seal_write`, `pending_deletes`, `meta_pool_wait`, `round_commit`, `handoff_reclaim`, `manifest_deletes`, `namespace_cleanup`, `ref_object_cleanup`, `orphan_sweep`.
When the frontier is not complete, destructive work is suppressed pool-wide because blob in-degree is pool-wide and there is no ownership partition of the blob space.

`suppress_destructive` is computed as `!report.anomalies.empty() || !carried_holds.empty() || frontier_incomplete`; the authoritative flip changes only the value of `universe_authoritative` in the `frontier_complete` expression.
An authoritative empty universe is not a complete frontier: `frontier_namespaces > 0` is required so `0 == 0` cannot open destructive work.

The production destructive gate is complete only when `universe_authoritative` is true, `frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces`; `suppress_destructive` is then `!report.anomalies.empty() || !carried_holds.empty() || frontier_incomplete`.

At the destructive gate call site, `!suppress_destructive` implies `frontier_complete`, which implies `universe_authoritative`; therefore `planManifestCursorPage` receives an authoritative recovery argument whenever the gate opens.
The frontier instrumentation adds no backend requests; its normal per-namespace cost is one `uint8_t` store, and formatting occurs only inside the already-suppressed path when the deficit is nonzero.

When the graduation or redelete budget is exhausted, `settleEntry` carries the entry in `still_retired` unchanged: a condemned entry remains condemned, and a `delete_pending` entry remains `delete_pending` for a later round.
